intervals.label: cyclotron in use
intervals.note: 1950 is the earliest dated use of the Nevis cyclotron found, not a founding date. The laboratory is described in the present tense on its own site, so it is active.
intervals.quote: In 1950, John Tinlot and I had been pondering how to get pions into the cloud chamber.

name: Nevis Laboratories
notes: The cyclotron is not an Atlas accelerator record (not assigned to this stream); the experiment records it in a note. The facility's founding date was not found: the first dated use of the machine in the sources is Lederman's 1950 pion-beam work.

operator_text.quote: Nevis Labs is a physics research facility operated by Columbia University's Physics Department.

summary.plain: Columbia University's particle-physics laboratory at Irvington, New York. Its cyclotron gave physicists beams of pions and muons, and in January 1957 it was where Garwin, Lederman and Weinrich showed that parity is violated in pion and muon decay.
summary.technical: Columbia Physics Department's Nevis Laboratories, Irvington-on-Hudson, New York; hosted a 400 MeV synchrocyclotron (external pion and muon beams from about 1950).
